result.markdown: # S3 Buckets {.unnumbered} This is the third part of lab 7. It assumes you've set up your AWS group, user, configured the CLI, created an S3 bucket, and pushed the penguin `vetiver` model data.[^lab7-part-02] [^lab7-part-02]: If you haven't completed these steps, please see [Getting started with AWS](start-aws.qmd) and [EC2 Buckets](aws-ec2.qmd) ## Creating S3 buckets We can use the `s3api` command to create the S3 bucket for the `penguin-vetiver-model-data`. ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3api create-bucket \ --bucket penguin-vetiver-model-data \ --region us-east-1 \ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: These commands are pretty straightforward, but you can also read more in the documentation. Note that bucket names must be globally unique. The response from the API should be something like the following: ```json { "Location": "/penguin-vetiver-model-data", "BucketArn": "arn:aws:s3:::penguin-vetiver-model-data" } ``` We can also see this in the dashboard by looking up **S3** resources: ![General purpose S3 bucket](img/lab7-s3-bucket-dashboard.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} ## Pushing the models to S3 Now that we've created an S3 bucket, we can push the respective Python/R model data into their locations. I'd like to keep the same `Python/` and `R/` respective folders, which I can do with the commands below. ### R model From the `do4ds-labs/_labs/lab07` folder: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 cp R/api/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/R/models/ \ --recursive \ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: ### Python model From the `do4ds-labs/_labs/lab07` folder: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 cp Python/api/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/Python/models/ \ --recursive \ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: ### Copy vs. sync It might make more sense to use `sync` instead of copy. `sync` only uploads new/changed files, which might be better for repeated deploys: **`R/`**: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 sync R/api/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/R/models/ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: **`Python/`**: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 sync Python/api/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/Python/models/ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: ### Verify We can verify the model data has been put in the S3 bucket at the command line: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 ls s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/ --recursive --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: We can also see this in the dashboard under **Amazon S3** > **Buckets** ![S3 bucket with penguin model data](img/lab7-s3-bucket-upload.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} #### Note on `vetiver` convention If using `pins` with an S3 board, `vetiver`/`pins` manages the folder structure automatically (versioned by timestamp/hash, like we already have locally). In that case we'd use: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} board <- pins::board_s3(bucket = "penguin-vetiver-model-data", prefix = "R/") vetiver::vetiver_pin_write(board, model) ``` ::: This is preferred over manual `cp`/`sync` if we want `vetiver`'s versioning and metadata to work correctly when later reading the model back with `vetiver_pin_read()`.
